rationale: Both correctly validate the core codes.audio fix, but neither flags the human reviewer's stale-docstring point. Y goes further by tracing the containment-fallback-vs-escalation interaction with a concrete live consumer (test_higgs_audio_v3.py) and investigating the legacy-vs-nested precedence question the human reviewer raised, giving it better recall; it also finds a genuine dead-code branch and magic-number duplication. X's two findings (unconditional containment loosening, vacuous short_text check) are solid and slightly more cleanly grounded, but Y's extra claims about issue #4949's specific failing tests/transcripts are unverifiable from the diff and drag its precision down somewhat. Both are concrete and file/line-anchored, with Y marginally more actionable given its specific code-level fixes.
